claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features hand-drawn black and white artwork with a sketchbook style.

citations.review_text:
I liked the music, I liked the visuals, I did not enjoy the plot, which consequently diminished my enjoyment of the gameplay itself.

The plus sides are that the game is gorgeous, the UI is smooth and intuitive, the art is magnificent, and they put love into it, and you can tell so. I hate to bemoan any game because it's like crapping on someone's life work, ya know? They made a beautiful game here and I am sad I didn't enjoy it.

I was attracted to this game by the recommendations of others, offered up for my enjoyment of games such as The Stanley Parable, Disco Elysium, Life is Strange, and the Telltale Walking Dead. I just didn't get it, I think, so I do not recommend this game if you are looking for spiritual successors to the games above. 

If you're looking for a visual novel about horror and love, this is a good pick, I just wish I got something more from it. Maybe I will return to it again one day, but I was ultimately more frustrated than entertained by my experience, which is why I do not recommend it.

I've only just started playing, but wow, this one grabbed me fast. The premise sounds almost too simple: you walk to a cabin in the woods and you're told to slay a princess to save the world. And somehow that one line unfolds into something way stranger and smarter than I expected.

The first thing that got me is the art. Hand-drawn black and white, like a sketchbook come to life, and that rough, unfinished quality makes everything feel tense and alive.

The voice acting is the other thing I keep thinking about. The Narrator in your ear trying to steer you, and the Voice of the Hero in your own head arguing back, create this constant little tug of war. A few times I just sat there listening instead of clicking anything.

But the part I'm already in love with is how the game treats choice. My decisions actually seem to reshape the story, and the Princess herself, right in front of me. I'm not following a script, I'm shaping one, and I can tell every playthrough is going to look completely different.

I'm still early in, so no spoilers from me, but honestly, it already feels less like playing a game and more like a long, unsettling conversation with myself. Really excited to see where it goes.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the voice acting features a mismatch between British accents for the narrator and hero roles and an American accent for the princess role.

citations.review_text:
[The Positive]
There is so many actions that leads to so many endings. It's really refreshing to see a visual novel that tries gage the players thoughts and reactions and give them an action that the player will most likely think or want to do depending on the scenario. It's also a nice feeling to play an ending and want to go back and see what you could do instead to see the alternative scenario.

[The Negative]
Why do you cast a british voice actor for the narrator and the multiple voices of the hero but THEN have an american girl do the voice of the princess. It's immersive breaking to hear two different accent. Also I'm not throwing any shades at the british voice actor since he's done a phenominal job but the princess voice is so bad to my ears that it makes me cringe listening to it and breaks the immersion.

[The Conclussion] 
I really enjoyed it. It may look like i don't have a lot of hours on it but i played a copy of the game somewhere else before playing it on Steam.
7/10 (-1 because of the voice acting of the princess)


If you are going to play this game, i suggest muting the princess voice muted because it's making this game worse than it really is.
Amazing. The narrators voice is perfect.

citations.review_text: I didn't know that a video game could make powers of 2 scary. Very good story, art, and voice acting by some incredible people.

I don't think I ever wanted more content for a game. 
Slay the Princess was something I picked up merely because I overheard this lady at Starbucks tell her coworker about the game, specifically the stranger route. I didn't even try it until now which is 2 years later from that moment but wow. I should've played it sooner so i would've forgotten everything and had the chance to play it again. 
The voice acting makes the game extremely immersive and the dialogue is very engaging. its a shame getting all the endings takes only about 10 hours because I could do this for 100 more hours. I would go as far to 100% the game even.
I don't believe there is anything out there quite like this story and honestly I'm not sure I'll see anything come close to it for awhile. I'd recommend it to everyone, even if some of the themes in the game take a little more effort to comprehend I had to stop and ponder a few times. This game is a handmade gift and whoever plays it is the recipient.
A lovely light horror game with excellent graphics and voice acting

Choice rich visual novel with fully voiced vo. Took me 3.5hrs for fullplaythrough to post credits: blind (besides trailer on store page) without skipping any dialog. Nowhere near 100% completion, but I feel satisfied.

I really, really loved playing this game. I enjoyed it so much I had a couple people who never play video games try it out, just so I could see their reactions, and the paths that they would pick. How similar would we be? *Some slight spoilers ahead.*

I wasn't let down, everyone I got to try it enjoyed it, and I got to experience this great game a couple of times through. The art is absolutely gorgeous, the sound effects and music are stunning, and the plot is so good you can enjoy it over and over and over again. The choices and paths are basically unlimited, you can pick different options on a repeat path and see something completely different, and I am sure that there are things I never saw still waiting in the game to be discovered.

It is an easy game to play, a choose your own adventure that is super atmospheric and creepy, and yet has no issues flipping on a dime to be wonderful, or even awe inspiring. However, disgusting and uneasy and scary are certainly what I feel like was done the best.

The voice actors should all be extremely proud of themselves, doing so many different voices and versions of voices, those different versions expressing different emotions. I looked through all of the awards this game got, it is certainly deserving of them all, but in this day of AI and sloppy performances, there should be some kind of award and recognition for the VAs. They really make the game shine.

I would highly recommend this game, even if you are not a fan of horror. There are no jump scares, it is just extremely well done atmospheric and psychological horror. Normally, having only been able to get twelves hours of of this game, with other people also having played it to give it more hours, I would say that you should get it on sale. But, that would be with normal games, that don't have hundreds if not thousands of hand drawn images, and thousands, if not reaching ten thousand, lines of dialogue. This game is a work of art, and if it interests you and it is not …

citations.review_text: This game is very fun, many different choices and endings unique to you! The art is beautiful, along with the soundtrack. Every character has an in-depth personality, so you are bound to find one you can empathize and relate to in someway. After completing my first playthrough, I have to say the replay-ability is amazing, and I enjoy trying to collect the achievements, instead of it feeling like a chore. Thank you devs for creating a lovely game!

This game is very well thought-through and interactive. The art design is amazing, the voice lines are great, and the music just pulls it altogether so nicely. If you're looking for a game that has an intriguing storyline and deeper meaning, then look no further. I've watched play-through's of this game after my friend introduced me to the game on his computer. Since then, I've been attempting to play it on my own computer and it has not failed to impress me yet. If you do decide to play, good luck ACTUALLY escaping this world OR slaying the princess. Believe me, there's a lot of twists.

This game is something else. It gives you memories and feelings you'd never expect from a game these days. The beautiful artwork feels comforting, the voice acting feels soothing, the OST is bittersweet, and the story... well, the story is the most beautiful part of this game.

I can't tell you much about this story without spoiling it. The best I can say is that, "You're on a path in the woods. And at the end of that path is a cabin. And in the basement of that cabin is a princess. You're here to slay her. If you don't, it will be the end of the world."

Go play this game with this amount of information about the story. Going in blind is and will always be the best way to play this game. This game is and will probably remain as one of my favorite visual novel games on the current market of video games. I'd rate this game a 11/10. 

The rest of what I'd say will be a spoiler. Don't read the rest unless you've already played the game. but take my word.. this game is worth the money and It's very replayable and not "the annoying kind of replayable" if you get what I mean.

My second favorite feature would be the endless endings you get, and the third would be the endless consequences there are. One of my consequences is an ending, and the ending, the very first ending I've got through this playthrough, is "A New and Unending Dawn, and everyone hates you." Long story short, everyone hates me. :( I think I've got that enndig because I was not sympathetic with the voices every time I went to the Long Quiet, and I'm still very confused about the story of this game. But I'll continue playing it to understand more. Wish me luck. [/spoiler]

citations.review_text:
10/10 - Emotionally and existential flashbang.
This game has the capacity to alter you.

It's given me a different perspective on some of life's experiences. 
An experience best left unspoiled - if you're unsure. Go for it. There horror is well done and serves to enhance the narrative. Even those of a semi-nervous disposition shouldn't be dissuaded.

The feelings it leaves you with are complicated - but makes you richer for having experienced it.
A lovely light horror game with excellent graphics and voice acting

One of the best stories I've experienced.

Things to expect:
- A lot of horror elements, particularly existential horror
- Confusion...
- Philosophy
- Being humbled

I feel everything else is probably best experienced blind, and taken in. It's a weird game, it's out there, but it's excellent.

I look forward to getting more of the endings/paths and may update my review.

i previously completed my first playthrough outside of steam, back before the pristine cut released. Slay the Princess is absolutely one of those games that you NEED to go into blind. 

understand that this IS a horror game, in the sense that there is horror, but every step you take is intentional. there are no "cheap scares", no scenes added just for the sake of shock or disgust. 

the game will tell you this as soon as you boot it up. it is a love story. see it through. it will take more forms than you would think a love story could, and thats part of the beauty.

phenomenal game, truly. I was left in absolute horror each time and with each attempt became more and more desperate. I could feel that desperation then turn into anger and I found myself making darker decisions than I had before, thinking I could simply end the game-- even THEN having more choices to choose from. so so great

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive voice acting across its dialogue, with performances described as exceptional by multiple players.

citations.review_text:
Hauntingly Beautiful.
    Slay the Princess is one of maybe two video games I've played that I would strongly desire to hold and read in novel format. I thoroughly enjoy its rapid fire thought experiment format. Its oscillates between horrifically bitter to perfectly sanguine. The game also features astounding voice acting; Sims' especially. Goodnight's performance is not as strong but is still impressive.
    Includes all essential visual novel QOL features.
    Most of the soundtrack is functional and not meant to take one's attention. However, the main few tracks, such as the main theme and some character themes still keep me up at night by embodying "hauntingly beautiful".
    STP drags you to every corner of the known philosophical landscape and back to then asks you, with it's fist tightened around the collar of your shirt, "what exactly is your takeaway?"

Slay the Princess is a horror visual novel about a hero sent to kill an all-powerful princess before she ends the world. This game has such a unique approach to horror, and its combination of psychological and gore horror is exquisite. The hand-drawn black-and-white art style works well to emphasize the horror, and collecting the CGs from the various routes feels satisfying. The voice acting is superb: each delivery beautifully emphasizes the horror or the surreal humor. The story is abstract enough that it's fun to speculate on its meaning. The game reads to me as a metaphor for trauma, and it handles this sensitive matter in a graceful and poignant way. While I wish there was more direction for the first couple playthroughs, once you get into a groove and understand the game's formula, this is such a great unsettling visual novel with lovely art and a lot of heart behind it.

A dark and gloomy game that even if you’re not a fan of visual novels is still absolutely worth it.

The premise is a unique take on the genre similar to Doki Doki Literature Club, where it goes beyond a simple story with a few choices that determine what happens. you can tell what you’re supposed to do from the title, but the way you go about slaying (if you even will) will show you unique interactions and events that don’t drain you while playing even after multiple playthroughs. The voice acting is incredible and displays the range of emotions for each character. Playing Slay The Princess is best experienced blind with no knowledge on the impact of your choices.

what a beautiful, unique, and heart wrenching game. i thought i was going to be overwhelmed by the amount of routes this game has, but i enjoyed every second of it. the hand drawn art is probably my favorite part of the whole thing. i was so impressed with all the different types of princesses and the care that clearly went into the design of each of them. the only thing that wasn’t quite for me was the voice acting. due to the length of the game and how often i had to replay routes, i started to become a bit irritated with it, so i turned it off. otherwise it was truly a phenomenal experience. i recommend this to everyone, whether you’re a fan of visual novels or not. it’s worth the read.

I bought Slay the princess almost two years ago exactly, I picked it up whilst it was on sale with a handful of other games, at the time I booted it up for maybe 10 minutes before deciding that I was in the mood to play something else. For two years it sat in my library and I paid it no mind until recently when I decided to have another look.

Let me say that this is a game that deserves to be played. I never would have expected this game to be what it is. I never thought that this would be one of my favourite games of all time, but here we are.

Slay the princess is a heart-wrenchingly beautiful experience, one that even now I struggle to put into words. If you can go into this game with as little knowledge as possible, then do so, look up nothing, let this wonderous piece of art speak for itself.

Slay the princess is a visual novel with a very basic concept but that has such immense breadth of character to it, I initially believed I was in for a short and sweet psychological horror but was met with one of the most compelling and hauntingly beautiful narratives I have ever experienced. The game so organically through it's masterful writing and genuinely gorgeous hand drawn art tackles themes of fate, death, suffering, love and tragedy. Combined with absolutely incredible performances by the voice actors, every single line of dialogue within this game, of which there are many thousands, is perfect. All of these elements are also accompanied by one of the most enchanting game soundtracks which, even after many, many hours never dulls in it's beauty.

I won't say anymore. I don't feel like I have it in my vocabulary to actually do this game justice in terms of a review and nor do I have the words to describe the intense and raw emotions which this game has made me feel, even now this game has a grip on my heart, and I don't want it to let go. 

My only regret is that I didn't play this game sooner, and now that it's done I only wish I could see more.

citations.review_text:
[proceed into the cabin]

what a beautiful, unique, and heart wrenching game. i thought i was going to be overwhelmed by the amount of routes this game has, but i enjoyed every second of it. the hand drawn art is probably my favorite part of the whole thing. i was so impressed with all the different types of princesses and the care that clearly went into the design of each of them. the only thing that wasn’t quite for me was the voice acting. due to the length of the game and how often i had to replay routes, i started to become a bit irritated with it, so i turned it off. otherwise it was truly a phenomenal experience. i recommend this to everyone, whether you’re a fan of visual novels or not. it’s worth the read.

This is an absolutely beautiful visual novel. The story is quite intriguing, with a message about life you don't see too often. It's also a nice little sub-genre. It's definitely horror, there's no doubt about that, but not jumpscare or mascot horror, both of which have become a bit of the "standard" as of late. I was incredibly enamored by this game, top to bottom. The replay loop feels great. Only at the last 3 gallery images did I start getting bored of going round and round to see different paths. Again can I say how beautiful this game is? The soundtrack and the art mesh great together. Visual novels only work well when they're visually appealing and feel good to read, and Slay the Princess is absolutely both. My only gripe is that sometimes I felt the Narrator spoke too slowly, but I can hardly complain when most other VNs of this caliber aren't fully voice acted.

100% worth the money and the time to play. Grab your pristine blade, and slay the princess.
